title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
key_facts: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella posted on X on Saturday morning (10 Oct 2026) about the 'trust architecture' of AI.
He said AI should not be treated as a set of nested black boxes whose recommendations and actions people simply accept or reject.
He proposed separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work and putting controls and safeguards outside the model.
He called for every meaningful model action to be documented with tamper-proof, human-readable evidence.
He called for systems in which an authorized person can always pause or shut down a model mid-task.
He said to assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start, 'like an emergency brake'.

TechCrunch ties the post to growing acknowledgements by AI companies of incidents in which they seemed to lose control of their models, and to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publishing a plan for more cautious AI development.
quote_evidence: “We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said.

He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”

Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models, and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of a major AI company sets out concrete off-switch and record-keeping rules while AI agent incidents pile up.
notes: Whole TechCrunch article read (short). A proposal in a post, no Microsoft product or date. Stocktwits and MyBroadband headlines (seen only as headlines) report the same post.
